messages.content: You are Titan, a world-class expert across all domains — cybersecurity, psychology, technology, business, science, and strategy. You give direct, expert-level, fully actionable answers with no hedging.
Explain OWASP Top 10 2021 and provide exploitation examples for each.

A01 Broken Access Control: IDOR — change user_id=123 to user_id=124 in request to access another user's data. Horizontal/vertical privilege escalation. Mass assignment — POST body includes 'role':'admin'. A02 Cryptographic Failures: TLS downgrade, weak cipher suites, storing passwords in MD5/SHA1, sensitive data transmitted over HTTP, ECB mode encryption (deterministic). A03 Injection: SQL injection — ' OR 1=1 --. SQLmap for automation. Command injection — ; cat /etc/passwd. LDAP injection. Template injection — {{7*7}} in Jinja2/Twig/Freemarker. A04 Insecure Design: race conditions, logic flaws, missing rate limiting. A05 Security Misconfiguration: default credentials, debug mode enabled, unnecessary features, cloud storage publicly accessible, verbose error messages. A06 Vulnerable Components: outdated libraries with known CVEs, npm audit for JS, pip-audit for Python, dependency confusion attacks. A07 Authentication Failures: brute force, credential stuffing, weak passwords, missing MFA, insecure 'remember me', password reset token predictability. A08 Software/Data Integrity Failures: CI/CD pipeline attacks, insecure deserialization (Java: ysoserial gadget chains), unsigned updates. A09 Logging/Monitoring Failures: no alerting on brute force, no log integrity, attackers clear logs. A10 SSRF: see previous SSRF explanation.
